title: What’s Behind Australia’s New $42 Million in Assistance to Ukraine?
author: Grant Wyeth
text:
Credit: Ukrainian Presidency
Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York this week. Out of that meeting came a new bilateral security agreement, unlocking a further US$42 million in Australian assistance to Ukraine – split between Australian Defense Force (ADF) equipment, Ukraine’s Energy Support Fund, and humanitarian assistance. This brings Australia’s total contribution to almost US$1.4 billion. Ukraine is obviously far away from Australia’s immediate security concerns in the Indo-Pacific, but Canberra’s support for the country is driven principally by its interest in preventing territorial conquest from becoming an accepted instrument of international relations. As a geographically isolated country with considerable economic interests beyond its immediate region, Australia depends on international rules that constrain the use of force. Canberra understands that allowing this principle to be undermined in Europe would weaken its application elsewhere, including in the Indo-Pacific. Alongside this is the position that smaller and middle-sized countries should retain the freedom to make their own security and diplomatic decisions.[...]
